caste.quote: We analyzed morphological trait variations in the workers of four common and phylogenetically distant ant species (Dinoponera quadriceps, Dorymyrmex goeldii, Pheidole radoszkowskii, and Ectatomma muticum) along disturbance and aridity gradients in the Caatinga dry forest.
For each species and plot, we measured between 3 and 10 (median = 5) randomly selected workers from the captured individuals.
Pheidole radoskowskii possesses minor and major worker castes; only minor workers were measured.

Morphometric traits used to characterize the morphological variation of workers of Dinoponera quadriceps, Dorymyermex goeldii, Pheidole radoskowskii, and Ectatomma muticum along our disturbance and aridity gradients in Catimbau National Park, Pernambuco state, NE Brazil

basisOfRecord.quote: Ants were collected using pitfall traps in 20 0.1-ha plots distributed over an area of 213.75 km 2 .

Traps were constructed from 12-cm-diameter plastic pots partially filled with an alcohol and ethylene glycol solution with detergent to preserve the sample and were activated for 48 h in March 2015 (for more details on ant sampling, see Arnan, Arcoverde, et al., 2018).

For each selected individual, we measured eight morphological traits that may respond to environmental changes and that are particularly sensitive to variations in aridity and chronic anthropogenic disturbances (Table 1).

Morphometric traits used to characterize the morphological variation of workers of Dinoponera quadriceps, Dorymyermex goeldii, Pheidole radoskowskii, and Ectatomma muticum along our disturbance and aridity gradients in Catimbau National Park, Pernambuco state, NE Brazil

For each species and plot, we measured between 3 and 10 (median = 5) randomly selected workers from the captured individuals.

For each individual, we measured body size (Weber's length), eye length, antenna (scape + funicle) length, mandible length, clypeus length, leg (tibia +femur) length, inter-ocular distance, and pilosity (Table 1).
